title: Prove exact four-column capacity over fifteenth roots
body:
**Complete finite result: eight rows over fifteenth roots support exactly four orthogonal columns.** An explicit matrix attains four; a complete extension graph excludes five. This resolves the smallest attainment question left by [PR #7768](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7768), whose general defect bound permits five. **No new kappa** follows.

Read the [proof and attaining matrix](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6dbe6e9503f26189833d5ef213aee708679835f2/research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity/PROOF.md), [complete graph certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6dbe6e9503f26189833d5ef213aee708679835f2/research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity/RESULT.json), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6dbe6e9503f26189833d5ef213aee708679835f2/research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6dbe6e9503f26189833d5ef213aee708679835f2/research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6dbe6e9503f26189833d5ef213aee708679835f2/research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity/CREDITS.md).

Normalize any pair to a constant column and the exponent vector `(0,5,10,0,3,6,9,12)`. Of 20,160 possible normalized further columns, exactly 95 are orthogonal to this pair. Their compatibility graph has two six-cycles and 83 isolated vertices. It has no triangle, so three further columns cannot coexist. There are twelve normalized four-column sets; one is displayed and checked entry by entry. These are labeled counts for the fixed pair, not a classification under every matrix equivalence.

Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/fifteenth-root-column-capacity
```

Both registered modes print:

```text
PASS_FIFTEENTH_ROOT_COLUMN_CAPACITY
Exact maximum: four orthogonal columns in eight rows over fifteenth roots
116280 tail multisets; two enumerations of 20160 normalized columns; 95 extensions
4465 pairs; 138415 triples; graph = two six-cycles and 83 isolated vertices
Twelve normalized four-column sets; exact attaining Gram; 448 changed entries reject
```

The unchanged source census covers all 319,770 eight-root multisets and proves the pair normalization. The new seven-term-tail census and separate cycle-permutation enumeration agree on all candidates. Every pairing is checked by polynomial division and a separate tensor basis. Component traversal, all triples and edge common-neighbor bitsets independently exclude triangles. All 448 single-entry changes to the witness fail orthogonality; omitting conjugation gives the wrong graph.

Nineteen retained files are authenticated. The unchanged PR7762 and nested PR7744 verifiers, normal/optimized registered replay, syntax/indentation, committed bytes/source history/modes, export and sealed read-only Git-free serial replay pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44442275205/job/135285773928) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

Ali Romman (@aliromman) supplied the [general defect bound](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/PROOF.md) and [open question](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/fefebaf8285f3c46f75a815657acbf48780763fb/research/mixed-cycle-column-defect/README.md), and the [finite census checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/d33fe8562c86888307cbba4a2aa92490212c8d78/research/mixed-cycle-column-obstruction/verify.py) in [PR #7762](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7762). Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplied the original two-prime question in [PR #7744](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7744), with its [pinned proof and question](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7dc85513e8ee9b771a5856f027cf199936f85af0/research/two-prime-column-completion/README.md). All prior source notices, including the cycle theorem and atlas lineage, remain intact. The new finite capacity proof does not rely on the general spectral bound.

This result fixes the alphabet to fifteenth roots and the row count to eight. Roots of order `3*5^b` for b>1, other row counts, approximate orthogonality, full matrix-equivalence classification, physical preparation and complete caller costs remain open. All five framework assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged. The selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were not run. No independent human/formal-kernel acceptance or global literature priority is claimed.

Base: canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8. Source pins do not assert ancestry.
